claims.text: Applying a thin, adherent WS2 nanoparticle coating to a high-entropy alloy will produce an in-situ tribofilm during sliding.
The WS2 coating will lower the coefficient of friction relative to the untreated high-entropy alloy over a broad temperature range.
The WS2 coating will lower the wear rate relative to the untreated high-entropy alloy over a broad temperature range.
An approximately 1 μm WS2 nanoparticle layer can be deposited by PVD with uniform, adherent coverage on the alloy surface.
During use, the coating forms a continuous tribofilm consisting of aligned, layered WS2 structures.
The lamellar WS2 layers shear easily under sliding contact.
Easy shearing of the WS2 layers reduces friction.
The WS2 tribofilm acts as a physical barrier that minimizes abrasive wear.
The WS2 tribofilm acts as a physical barrier that minimizes adhesive wear.
WS2 remains sufficiently stable over the proposed temperature range to provide consistent lubrication.
The coating may reduce friction by approximately 30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating may reduce wear rate by approximately 50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention will remain effective during sliding wear in air at temperatures up to approximately 500°C.
Performance outside the tested temperature range or under substantially different environments is uncertain.
The long-term stability of the tribofilm at extreme temperatures or in oxidizing environments is unresolved.
